title: TimeLock Autoscale & Synapse Layer — Dedicated Capacity PRD (draft)
body:
Context and motivation:

Redwood’s Dedicated customers demand predictable throughput and clear isolation guarantees, but we need more flexible burst behavior to accommodate short spikes without compromising SLOs for other tenants. Current approaches (fixed reserved pools + ad-hoc burst credits) work but show two recurring pain points: (1) burst decisions occur with little time-bounded guarantees, causing long tail resource entanglement; (2) isolation controls are binary (on/off) and don’t express gradual fidelity degradation.

Proposal summary (one-liner):
Implement a TimeLock Autoscale system fronted by a lightweight orchestration plane we call the Synapse Layer: tenants can borrow temporally-bounded burst vouchers that provide elevated capacity/fidelity for short windows; the Synapse Layer enforces repayment constraints, progressive fidelity lanes, and an isolation-safe reclamation protocol.

Goals:
- Maintain per-tenant latency SLOs for reserved capacity while allowing safe, short-lived bursts above reservation.
- Provide deterministic, auditable windowed bursts (time-locked) to avoid long-term resource entanglement.
- Offer tiered fidelity controls (graceful quality degradation) that can be applied as capacity is reclaimed.
- Improve observability for burst usage and cross-tenant interference; make recovery and runbook actions straightforward.

Non-goals:
- Replace long-term committed capacity contracts.
- Support unlimited or unmetered burstings.

Key concepts and terminology:
- Voucher: a short-lived token representing permission to consume burst capacity for a fixed time window (e.g., 30s, 2min). Vouchers are granted by Synapse and bound to tenant, model-version, and route.
- Timelock: policy that ensures a voucher expires deterministically and is non-renewable until repayment/settle logic completes.
- Fidelity slices: ordered degradation profiles (full-quality, cached-prefetch, quantized-low, truncation heuristics) that can be applied to requests when capacity tightens.
- Cohort rebalancer: a periodic optimizer that reassigns warm-pools / prewarmed slots between tenants to reduce cold-starts while respecting vouchers.

High-level design:
1) Admission: A tenant’s request that would exceed reserved capacity routes to Synapse. Synapse consults policy (tier, current utilization, credit balance, historical burst behavior) and either: (a) issue a voucher (time-window, quota, allowed fidelity lanes); (b) queue to reserved lane; or (c) reject/fail fast.

2) Enforcement: Serving runtime accepts requests carrying vouchers and tags metrics with voucher-id and window expiration. The runtime enforces per-voucher caps (concurrency, token rate) and applies the fidelity lane assigned.

3) Timelock semantics: Vouchers are cryptographically signed and include expiry and version. They cannot be extended client-side. Synapse offers an optional short renewal channel that does stateful repayment accounting if tenant opts in (see repay flow).

4) Repayment & repayment-fallback: After voucher expiry Synapse reconciles usage vs. allowance. If a tenant overused, they enter a short soft-quarantine (token back-off, lower fidelity) and are placed on a cooldown. Persistent overuse triggers linear backoff and manager notification.

5) Isolation guards: When cross-tenant impact is detected (tail latency spike, GPU memory pressure), Synapse can preempt outstanding vouchers according to policy priority: first-in-last-out preemption within the same tier, cross-tenant preemption avoids degrading tenants that are within reserved capacity. Preemption triggers automated fidelity fallbacks and a graceful completion window (e.g., let present requests finish within 5s before hard drop).

Policy primitives (configurable per tenant/plan):
- Max voucher concurrency (vouchers simultaneously active)
- Max time-window options (e.g., 30s, 2m, 10m)
- Repayment mode: optimistic (post-check) vs enforced (charge/penalty)
- Fidelity ladder mapping (traffic percent -> fidelity slice)
- Preemption priority score (customer tier, SLA criticality, historical compliance)

Telemetry and observability:
- New telemetry tags: voucher-id, voucher-issue-time, voucher-expiry, fidelity-lane, repay-status, preempted-by, synapse-decision-reason.
- Dashboards: voucher usage heatmap by tenant, time-to-repayment histogram, post-burst tail-latency correlation.
- Alerts: sustained preemption rate > X% for pool Y; repeated overuse (3 violations in 24h).

Runtime changes (serving/runtime team):
- Token-level tagging plumbing in request path to carry voucher metadata.
- Enforcement hooks: per-request fidelity switch, quota checks against voucher allowance.
- Fast path for fidelity lanes implemented as light-weight request transforms (e.g., prefix trimming, forced stop tokens, quantized model selection).

Control plane (synapse) requirements:
- Low-latency decision API (<50ms p99) to avoid adding client latency.
- Durable ledger for voucher issuance and settlement (single source of truth).
- Cohort rebalancer optimizer that consumes pool utilization signals and reassigns prewarm slots nightly and on-critical events.

Billing/Accounting model:
- Voucher issuance tracked and billed as burst credits per second-of-capacity or per-token uplift depending on plan.
- Penalty model (optional for enterprise plans): overuse beyond voucher leads to premium billing or automatic denial of future vouchers.

Failure modes and mitigation:
- Race between expiry and in-flight requests: provide a grace window (5s) and passive enforcement where expired voucher requests are routed to a degraded fidelity lane instead of immediate hard fail.
- Synapse outage: fallback to conservative behavior — deny new vouchers and allow requests to continue only on reserved capacity. Alert and escalations.
- Malformed vouchers: runtime to validate cryptographic signature; on failure treat as no-voucher request.

Operational runbook (high level):
- Detect: dashboard shows rising preemption events or pool-level tail latency increase.
- Triage: inspect voucher heatmap, identify high-issuers, check repayment failures.
- Mitigate: temporarily disable voucher issuance for offending tenant cohorts; increase cohort isolation weight; activate manual preemption of lower-priority vouchers.
- Remediate: communicate to affected tenants, propose fidelity policy adjustments or recommend Dedicated capacity top-ups.

Rollout plan (phases):
1) Internal alpha (serving + infra): implement Synapse decision API + runtime tagging; test with synthetic tenants and chaos injection. (8 weeks)
2) Beta with select customers (3–5): enable voucher windows limited to 30s, repay-mode=optimistic, no penalties; monitor telemetry (6 weeks)
3) Gradual GA: expand window options, introduce repay penalties for enterprise contracts, expose controls in Console and API (10 weeks)

Key metrics to measure success:
- Reduction in reserved-pool SLO breaches during bursts (target: 60% fewer cross-tenant tail incidents)
- Mean time to reclaim capacity after burst (target: <30s)
- Voucher misuse rate (target: <2% of vouchers cause overuse penalties in first 6 months)
- Customer satisfaction for beta tenants (qual: post-burst application quality)

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- Should vouchers be billable per-second-of-GPU or per-token uplift? Hybrid billing increases complexity but aligns incentives.
- How to set default fidelity ladders that work well across diverse workloads (chat vs embeddings vs rerank)? We may need workload class heuristics.
- Cryptographic signing vs centralized ledger-only approach: signing improves safety for distributed runtimes but adds key management complexity.

Small engineering notes / TODOs:
- Define voucher token proto (fields: id, tenant, model, route, issue_ts, expiry_ts, concurrency_limit, signature).
- Add runtime hooks for fidelity lane transforms (short, common list for beta).
- Instrument end-to-end latency tracing for voucher lifecycle.
- Draft Console UX: voucher usage panel + ability to request manual emergency voucher.

Appendix: example flow (30s voucher)
1) Tenant traffic exceeds reserved lane threshold at t=0: Synapse issues 30s voucher v:123 -> allowed concurrency 50, fidelity: full.
2) Runtime accepts requests with v:123, logs voucher-id. At t=28s pool pressure spikes: Synapse signals preemption threshold.
3) Synapse preempts by refusing new acceptances for v:123, returning 5s grace. Runtime switches new requests to fidelity slice: cached-prefetch. Ongoing requests finish.
4) Voucher expires at t=30s; Synapse reconciles usage and notes no overuse. Voucher settled and recorded.

Contact and next steps:
- Lead: Asha Patel (product)
- Eng owners: Evan Liu (serving runtime), Priya Shah (infra), Jonah Rivera (observability)
- Action items: proto spec draft (Evan), Synapse decision API skeleton (Priya), fidelity lane library PoC (Jonah) — owners due by 2025-11-22.

Notes to reviewers:
This PRD is intentionally opinionated about time-bounded bursts (timelock) and fidelity slices to provide predictable reclamation semantics. Feedback sought on billing model and preemption priority heuristics.
